method: data/coverage/METHOD.md strict rule. paperStructure: One section of 50 questions (501 to 550): 40 stand-alone MCQs, then two passages with 5 questions each (541-545 liberalisation, 546-550 mass media); all 50 are printed and counted as asked.

facts: Social demography studies the wider causes and consequences of population structure and change (formal demography = measurement of components)

facts: Industrialisation (an industrial town set up among villages) physically brings urban life into a rural setup, unlike mass media, which carry images of urban life

Served material has the Rao three-impacts card (industrial town) but never says industrialisation transplants urban life physically; the served card fact-mass-media-rural-aspirations (media bring urban life styles to villages) even pulls a student towards the distractor Mass Media.

auditOfA.note: Every bank id A cited is in served_sociology.json and was read in full (stem, options, key, explanation); every card id is in data/keycards/decks/sociology.json and its front, back and NCERT quote were read. Each states what A attached to it; partial citations on not-covered items (Q16, Q18, Q21, Q23, Q25, Q32) teach only the part A claimed. Card suspension not read (see bankRead). One error in A's reasoning, not in a citation: A's Q23 reason says vaccination and sanitation are not taught; card fact-epidemic-control-measures states it (B added it). Q23 stays not covered on statement A alone.

ownSearchBeforeA.note: B wrote facts before opening A but did not record verdicts before reading A; after reading A, B re-derived every verdict from the material. B's first fact list counted Q49 (term not printed in the passage); settled to skill with A (the passage prints the idea; not a gap either way).

final.rule: Covered only if both A and B say covered; B's skill, off-syllabus and dropped labels win.

openCallsSettled.Q22 (n22): Covered: 1952, 1991, 2011 are dated by cards; knowing C (1952) precedes A (1991) alone selects option 3; the 2020 average-age card places D last.
openCallsSettled.Q40 (n40): Covered: every pair rests on a card; Chipko pair on two cards (women hugged trees; ecological concerns).
openCallsSettled.Q15 and Q32: Both are reachable by elimination from served material, but the deciding fact is not stated; kept not covered (doubtful = not covered), matching A.
openCallsSettled.Q23 (n23): Not covered on statement A only (famines caused by continuing poverty and malnutrition). Note the option set lets B, C true and D false force option 2, but METHOD requires every statement.

doNotAuthor.why: NCERT (and our served cards) define industrialisation as machine production and early modernisation as improvement in technology and production processes, so the textbook fits both to the keyed "new technology" item; the keyed industrialisation = market economy and westernisation = value systems pairs have no NCERT sentence. Authoring them would teach NTA's pairing against the textbook.

NCERT prints no date for the right-to-livelihood reading, the Van Panchayats or the RTI Act, and the NTA key puts Van Panchayats after the 1992 amendment although they date from the 1930s. No honest content teaches the keyed order.
